newsitem.title: FRANCE: Guinea's president open to second term in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Guinea's president open to second term in 1998.

text.p: Guinean President Lansana Conte, who seized power in 1984 and went on to win an election in 1993, is willing to stand for a second term in 1998 if called on by his party, he said in an interview published on Tuesday.

"If my party, which chose me as its candidate in 1993, wants my mission to continue and tells me it it has found no one to replace me, then we would discuss the matter and I would accept," he told the weekly Jeune Afrique.

"Our electoral laws state that a president cannot serve more than two terms. If the people give me a second term, I hope to have the time to take a rest afterwards before becoming too tired," he said.
Conte, who is 62, acknowledged his health was not perfect but said he was doing well enough to remain head of state.

"I have good enough health, enough vigour, to accomplish my missions, whether a mission of state or a family mission," he said, adding that he planned the next day to do manual work in his fields. "If I were sick, I couldn't do farm work," he said.

Conte, an army general who has been in power since taking the presidency by force in April 1984, said a bloody but unsuccessful army rebellion last February had reinforced his dislike for coup attempts.
"You know, I detest coups d'etat," he said. "You are going to tell me that in 1984, we carried out a coup d'etat. But that is not correct. We remedied a catastrophic situation."
